newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist leader blasts Moscow's Chechen deal.
newsitem.headline: Communist leader blasts Moscow's Chechen deal.

text.p: The leader of Russia's Communist opposition condemned on Sunday the Kremlin's new accord with Chechen separatist rebels, saying it spelled the break-up of the nation and demanding a vote of no-confidence in the government.

Gennady Zyuganov told Interfax news agency the accord signed on Saturday by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Aslan Maskhadov, leader of the rebel government, was "unconstitutional and de jure marks the beginning of the break-up of Russia".
As a prelude to the deal, President Boris Yeltsin reversed Kremlin policy and ordered the last two brigades of Russian troops out of the region before Chechen elections on January 27.
The deal, which came after nearly two years of war, stops short of granting Chechnya the full independence separatist leaders say they want.
But it does foresee giving the region considerable autonomy.
Zyuganov, who lost to Yeltsin in the July 3 presidential election, said he summoned an emergency meeting of leaders of his national-patriotic union coalition for Sunday morning.

He said the Constitutional Court and parliament should review the agreement, which he said "smells of a Belovezh Mark 2", referring to the treaty signed by Yeltsin and other leaders in December 1991 which formally broke up the Soviet Union.
The communists want to recreate the union in some form.
Movladi Udugov, one of the main Chechen negotiators of the accord, dismissed Zyuganov's objections.
"It's no surprise," he told Reuters. "If the agreement hadn't been signed yesterday he would be objecting too."
